STYLE: 1930s rubber hose cartoon, hand-inked cel animation look, original characters.
Thick uniform outline in dark plum #3D3346 on every shape, clean confident lines, no sketchy strokes.
Flat cel colors with at most one soft shade tone per color, no gradients on characters, no 3D rendering, no glossy plastic look; one small white highlight dot is allowed.
Characters: bendy rubber hose arms and legs with no elbows or knees, white four-finger cartoon gloves, big round shoes, pie-cut eyes (black ovals with a small wedge cut out), simple wide mouth, big head-to-body ratio.
Character colors are saturated: red #D2463C, blue #3E6DB5, yellow #F2C14E, cream #F4E6C8, glove white #FBF6EA.
Backgrounds and large props look like faded watercolor on paper in beige #CFAC8D, sand #D7BE97, dusty navy #4E546E, muted olive #8A9A6B, warm grey #907F77, and are LESS saturated than the characters.
Soft light from the top-left. No cast shadow on the ground. No text, letters or numbers anywhere.
Do not copy any existing cartoon or game character, logo, or scene.

Each item isolated on a flat solid #FF00FF magenta background (or transparent), full figure visible, nothing cropped, wide empty margin around every item, no ground line, no floor, no frame, no border, no shadow under the item.
Characters face the viewer at a slight high 3/4 angle unless a direction is given. "Side" always means facing RIGHT.

Strict side view for a 2D side-scrolling game, the camera is level with the ground (not from above). Characters face RIGHT.
Tiles and background layers marked "connect seamlessly" must match exactly at the LEFT and RIGHT edges so they can repeat.
Mid layers: draw only the lower part, leave the upper part empty flat #FF00FF magenta.

BARON VOLT: a huge villainous GENERATOR, the body is one big round-shouldered dynamo casing in dark copper #8A4B2A with brass #C99A3A bands and rivets.
His head is a tall glass-and-copper TESLA COIL crackling with small yellow sparks; under it a cream dial face with pie-cut eyes and a curled black WIRE MOUSTACHE.
His two arms are thick black cables ending in big brass PLUG hands with two prongs. A chest panel can swing open to show sockets.
Short thick legs with black boots. About three times BOGLE's height. Arrogant, greedy, funny-villain, never gory.

Exactly FIVE isolated full-body poses of the SAME Baron Volt, ONE horizontal row, left to right in listed order, generous equal magenta gutters. Wide landscape 3:1 sheet, each character about 500 pixels tall or larger. Same copper generator casing, tall glass/copper coil, cream face, wire moustache, brass plug hands, short black boots in every pose. Entire effects stay in their own slot. All faces, boots and actions point LEFT. Readable simple cel art, no scenery. In slam pose both cable arms end in two-prong brass plugs touching an invisible ground, sparks but NO floor line. In magnet pose both hands become horseshoe magnets. Coolant comes from a SIDE PIPE, not the mouth. Battery bowling is an underhand release toward LEFT.

Use case: stylized-concept. Game sprite sheet. Input references: style_anchor is primary palette/ink reference; ref_02 is technique ONLY, never copy its character, cup shape, lettering or logo; boss_idle sets villain tone only, do not copy clock anatomy. JOB-18 direction exception overrides the fixed RIGHT instruction above: EVERY item faces LEFT. Use pure flat #FF00FF background, no labels, no text, no numbers, no ground/shadow. Individual descriptions follow unchanged in order:
BARON VOLT standing tall and smug facing LEFT, plug arms crossed, coil head crackling with small sparks, wire moustache curled
BARON VOLT slamming both plug-shaped fists into the floor facing LEFT, bright sparks bursting from the floor, furious face
BARON VOLT facing LEFT with both arms stretched forward, his plug hands turned into horseshoe magnets, curved pull lines, greedy grin
BARON VOLT facing LEFT spraying a stream of blue coolant water from a pipe on his side onto the floor, smug
BARON VOLT facing LEFT bowling a big grey battery with a lit fuse along the floor with one arm, sly grin
records.reason: Slam and magnet bounding boxes overlap during slicing.
